title: Weakly associated primes detect the zero divisors of a ring
statement: Let A be a commutative ring [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Define WeakAss(A) to be the set of prime ideals that are minimal over the annihilator of some element of A. Then the set of zero-divisors of A is the union of the primes in WeakAss(A); equivalently, the complement of the union of WeakAss(A) is the set of non-zero-divisors of A.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.66.7, tag 05C3 (lemma-weakly-ass-zero-divisors), with M = R, union of weakly associated primes is the set of zero-divisors; definition of WeakAss: Definition 10.66.1, tag 0547

proof.text: Here f in A is a zero-divisor when fy = 0 for some nonzero y in A. Suppose f is a zero-divisor, with fy = 0 and y != 0. The ideal I = Ann(y) is proper, since 1 is not in I, and f lies in I. Hence V(I) is nonempty (Stacks tag 00E0), and by Zorn's lemma applied to the primes containing I, ordered by reverse inclusion (the intersection of a chain of primes is a prime containing I), there is a prime q minimal over I. Then f lies in I, which is contained in q, and q is in WeakAss(A). So every zero-divisor lies in the union of WeakAss(A).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 10.66.7 (tag 05C3), second half, specialized to M = A; tag 00E0

proof.text: Conversely, let f lie in a prime q that is minimal over I = Ann(y) for some y in A. The primes of the ring (A/I)_q correspond to the primes of A containing I and contained in q, so q(A/I)_q is the only prime of (A/I)_q, which is therefore a minimal prime. By Stacks tag 00EU the image of f in (A/I)_q is nilpotent, so there are g in A with g not in q and n > 0 with f^n g in I, that is f^n g y = 0. Since I is contained in q, g is not in I, so gy != 0. Take n >= 1 minimal with f^n g y = 0; then z = f^(n-1) g y is nonzero and fz = 0, so f is a zero-divisor. Together with the preceding step, the set of zero-divisors of A is the union of the primes in WeakAss(A).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 10.66.7 (tag 05C3), first half, specialized to M = A; tag 00EU

proof.text: By definition an element is a non-zero-divisor precisely when it is not a zero-divisor. Taking complements in the equality of the preceding two steps gives that the complement of the union of WeakAss(A) is the set of non-zero-divisors of A.
